q: What does Harbour Line Renovations do?
a: We renovate kitchens, bathrooms, ensuites and laundries across Perth, and take on whole-home and multi-room renovations and alfresco areas. We are a family-run company based in Osborne Park, in business since 2009, with our own designers and project managers. Plumbing, gas and electrical work is done by licensed tradespeople.

q: Which suburbs do you work in?
a: Greater Perth within roughly 30 km of Osborne Park: the coastal north (Scarborough, Trigg, Hillarys, Joondalup and nearby), the western suburbs (Cottesloe, Claremont, Nedlands, Subiaco), the inner city and north-east (Mount Lawley, Leederville, Maylands, Victoria Park), and south of the river (Fremantle, Applecross, Melville, Willetton, Rockingham). Outer suburbs such as Ellenbrook, Baldivis, Armadale and Mandurah only for whole-home jobs over $80,000, case by case. We do not work in regional Western Australia.

q: Is Harbour Line a real company?
a: No. Harbour Line Renovations is a fictional business created for a portfolio demonstration of an AI enquiry agent, built by Eklavya Shetty. Nothing here is a real quote or booking.

q: What is included in a kitchen renovation?
a: Design, demolition, cabinetry, benchtops, splashback, plumbing and electrical changes, lighting, installation of your chosen appliances, making good walls and flooring where needed, and a final clean. Painting and new flooring beyond the kitchen footprint are quoted as options. Everything included and excluded is listed in your written quote.

q: What is included in a bathroom or ensuite renovation?
a: Strip-out, waterproofing, tiling, vanity, shower, bath if wanted, toilet, tapware, heated towel rail, lighting, exhaust ventilation, plumbing and electrical work, and a final clean. Waterproofing is certified and backed by our 7-year structural and waterproofing workmanship warranty.

q: Do you do laundries?
a: Yes. A laundry renovation covers cabinetry, benchtop, tiling, the tub and appliance connections. Many clients do the laundry together with a bathroom to save on setup and trades. Typical range is $8,000 to $18,000 and 2 to 3 weeks on site.

q: Can you move walls or change my layout?
a: Non-structural walls can usually be removed or moved as part of a whole-home or kitchen renovation. If a wall is load-bearing, an engineer inspects and designs the change and any approval needed is lodged before work starts. We confirm what is possible at the site visit.

q: Do you build extensions, granny flats or new homes?
a: No. We focus on renovations of existing homes, plus roofed alfresco areas attached to the house. We do not build new homes, granny flats or second-storey additions.

q: Do you do standalone painting, flooring or landscaping?
a: Not as stand-alone jobs. Painting and flooring are included when they are part of a kitchen, bathroom or whole-home renovation. We do not take pool, roofing or landscaping jobs.

q: Do you do emergency repairs?
a: No. We are a planned renovation company, not a call-out service, so we cannot attend burst pipes, floods or electrical faults. In an emergency, call a licensed emergency plumber or electrician, or 000 if anyone is in danger. If damage is later repaired through an insurance claim, our team can talk with you separately about renovating afterwards.

q: How much does a kitchen renovation cost in Perth?
a: Typical ranges from past Perth jobs, including GST: a refresh with new doors, benchtop and splashback in the same layout is $18,000 to $30,000. A full renovation with mid-range finishes is $30,000 to $55,000. Premium finishes or a layout change run $55,000 to $95,000. These are ranges, not quotes. The firm number comes with the written quote after a site measure.

q: How much does a bathroom or ensuite renovation cost?
a: Typical ranges, including GST: standard $15,000 to $25,000, mid-range $25,000 to $38,000, premium or layout change $38,000 to $60,000. Moving the toilet or shower position, tiling to the ceiling and freestanding baths push the price up. A firm price comes only with a written quote after a site measure.

q: How much does a whole-home renovation cost?
a: A renovation of two to four rooms typically runs $80,000 to $220,000 including GST, depending on scope, finishes and the age of the home. The site visit and written quote give the real figure.

q: How much does an alfresco or outdoor living area cost?
a: A roofed area with paving and lighting typically costs $20,000 to $60,000 including GST, depending on size, roof type and whether it has an outdoor kitchen. Approvals are handled as part of the job.

q: What drives the price up or down?
a: Layout changes, moving plumbing or electrical points, cabinetry style, stone or tile choice, access (stairs, apartments, tight driveways), the age of the home and anything hidden once walls are opened. Keeping the same layout and choosing standard-size products keeps cost down.

q: Is the site visit and quote really free?
a: Yes. The site measure and quote visit costs nothing and carries no obligation. A designer spends about 60 to 90 minutes at your home, measures up and talks through your ideas.

q: Is the quote a fixed price?
a: Yes. The written quote is a fixed price with inclusions, exclusions and any allowances listed. If you ask for a change, or something unforeseen is found behind walls, it is priced and agreed in writing before it goes ahead. We cannot give a fixed price before the site measure.

q: Can I get a discount or have you match another quote?
a: Prices are set from the written quote after a site measure. Requests to adjust a price or compare it with another quote are handled personally by our team, not by this chat. I can pass your request to them.

q: What is the process from enquiry to handover?
a: One, enquiry. Two, a free site measure and quote visit. Three, a written fixed-price quote within 5 to 7 working days. Four, design and selections once you accept. Five, contract and deposit. Six, the build, run by a named project manager with weekly updates. Seven, handover with a walk-through, defect list, care guide and warranty paperwork.

q: How do I book a site visit?
a: I can book it here. Tell me your first name, suburb and what you are planning, then pick a time. Visits run Monday to Saturday in business hours, Perth time, and need a phone number or email so the designer can confirm. Visits are booked at least 24 hours ahead.

q: What should I have ready for the site visit?
a: Nothing is required. Photos, inspiration pictures, any plans you have and a rough idea of budget and timing all help. Someone who can make decisions for the home should be there. The visit takes about 60 to 90 minutes.

q: Who will be on site and who do I talk to during the job?
a: A named project manager runs your job, sends weekly progress updates and is your single point of contact. Licensed tradespeople carry out the plumbing, gas and electrical work.

q: Do I need to move out during the renovation?
a: Not for most bathroom, laundry or alfresco jobs. During a kitchen renovation you will have no kitchen for several weeks, and we set up a temporary arrangement where we can. Whole-home jobs often need you out for part of the build. We talk through it at the site visit.

q: How long does a renovation take?
a: From signing to starting on site is typically 3 to 6 weeks. On site: bathroom or ensuite 3 to 5 weeks, laundry 2 to 3 weeks, kitchen 4 to 8 weeks, alfresco 4 to 8 weeks, and whole-home 10 to 24 weeks. Custom cabinetry and imported stone can lengthen lead times.

q: How soon can you start?
a: Usually 3 to 6 weeks after the contract is signed, after the site visit, quote, design and selections. If you need to finish by a date such as Christmas, tell us early so we can plan backwards. We never promise a finish date before the quote is accepted.

q: Are you licensed and insured?
a: Yes. We hold the builder registration and contractor registrations required in Western Australia for our work, and plumbing, gas and electrical work is done by licensed tradespeople for those trades. We carry public liability and contract works insurance and, for larger jobs, arrange the home indemnity insurance required by Western Australian law. Current registration details are available at the site visit.

q: What warranty do you give?
a: 7 years on structural and waterproofing workmanship and 2 years on all other workmanship and finishes. Manufacturer warranties on products such as appliances, tapware and stone are passed to you and vary by product. Warranty claims go through the office, who book an inspection.

q: How do payments work?
a: Payments are staged and tied to progress, never paid in full upfront. A deposit of 5% on signing, progress payments at set milestones, and the final 5% on handover after the walk-through and defect list. For example, on a $28,000 kitchen: $1,400 deposit, about $8,400 at each of three milestones, and $1,400 at handover. Your contract sets the exact milestones.

q: Which payment methods do you accept?
a: Bank transfer or card. Card payments over $5,000 may carry a surcharge, so bank transfer is usually cheaper for larger stages.

q: Do you have a showroom and what are its hours?
a: Yes. Unit 6, 41 Tannery Lane, Osborne Park, with samples of benchtops, tiles, tapware and cabinetry. Open Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm and Saturday 9:00 am to 1:00 pm, closed Sunday and public holidays. Walk-ins are welcome, or book a time so a designer is free. The phone number is (08) 5550 0142.

q: I think there may be asbestos in my home. Can you help?
a: If asbestos is suspected, we do not disturb it. Work stops until it is tested and, if confirmed, removed by a licensed asbestos removalist, then our renovation continues. Asbestos questions are passed to our team, who can explain the steps for your home.

q: Can I have a freestanding bath, a walk-in shower or a heated towel rail?
a: Yes, all three are common options in bathroom and ensuite renovations. A freestanding bath usually adds cost because of the floor loading, plumbing position and extra waterproofing, so we check the space at the site visit. A heated towel rail is part of our standard bathroom inclusions. Prices stay inside the ranges quoted for the tier you choose, and the written quote after the site measure sets the final figure.

q: Can you do renovations that are being paid for by an insurance claim?
a: Insurance repair jobs are not part of what this chat handles. Our team can talk with you about whether a job fits, so I pass those questions to a person.
